approach: Root cause: the check stage keeps a baseline of failures present on the base commit (`Baseline`, `is_pre_existing`, `failure_split` at crates/athena-core/src/verify.rs:203-222), but nothing maps the file paths in a failing check's output to the paths the job changed. A failure that comes from a concurrent merge or an unrelated config or doc change is not in the baseline, so it reads as the job's own. The verifier's brief shows a locally run failing check as a name and a note only, because `check_result_view` (verify.rs:62-88) fills the tail and test names only for reused CI results. Fix at those two inputs, with no new rule. (1) verify.rs gets a pure function `failure_paths(check, changed_paths)` that pulls repository paths (`file:line:col` forms) out of a failed check's `output_tail` and splits them into those the job changed and those it did not. A second function turns that into one Minor Athena finding. (2) `judge` adds that finding for each blocking check, beside the existing newly-failing finding (verify.rs:447-472); reasons, severities and the verdict stay as they are. (3) `verification_stage` (run/verification.rs) computes the changed paths before the verifier's inputs are built, and puts the same finding text into the `detail` of each blocking failed check's `CheckResultView`. The brief already prints `detail` in parentheses (briefs.rs:1449-1460), so briefs.rs does not change. When the changed-path list is empty, no claim is made. The change adds unit tests, an end-to-end run test, a CHANGELOG entry and a new decision D186.

decisions.choice: Give the verdict inputs and the verifier brief a finding that links the failing output's paths to the job's changed paths. Add no refusal rule.
decisions.reason: The failing stage lacked that link. The verifier is shown no output for a locally run failing check (check_result_view fills the tail only when `r.reused`, verify.rs:75-86), and `judge` has the changed paths (VerdictInputs.changed_paths, verify.rs:167) but never compared them with the output. Giving the information can prevent the failure, so no refusal is allowed. The finding is Minor, so `serious` (verify.rs:652-655) and the reasons are unchanged and the expected share of newly refused readings is 0%.

rejected.option: Run the failing test again on the base tree and mark it pre-existing, as the introspections propose
rejected.why: The baseline per test already exists (verify.rs:203-211). A concurrent-change failure does not fail on the old base, so a base rerun cannot separate it. It also needs a new run stage and snapshot, which is much larger.

rejected.option: Excuse or downgrade a failure whose paths the job did not change
rejected.why: This would be a new verdict rule that changes what passes. Output paths are not proof of cause: a test can fail on a file the job did not touch because of what the job did. The request asks for information, not a rule.

rejected.option: Add a field to CheckResultView and render it in crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs
rejected.why: The existing `detail` field is already rendered for every check (briefs.rs:1449-1460). A new field would touch a second crate and the brief-shape tests for no gain.

rejected.option: Change `check_result_view` or `CheckRun` to carry the paths
rejected.why: CheckRun is a stored record type (athena-data records.rs:868). Changing it risks old-record parsing and `check_record_file`. The paths can be computed from `output_tail` when needed.

decisions.choice: One function builds the finding, and both `judge` and the brief detail use it. The cited-path extractor accepts only relative paths with an allow-listed extension (rs, toml, md, json, yml, yaml, txt, sh, lock). It drops paths starting with `/`, `~` or `target/`, paths containing `..`, URLs and duplicates, and caps the list at 10. A path counts as changed when it equals a changed path or a changed path ends with `/<path>`.
decisions.reason: A single source keeps the verdict's finding and the verifier's brief in step. The allow-list and the exclusions keep test names (`tests::a`), durations (`1.5s`), registry and rustc paths and build output from showing up as 'paths the job did not change'. The suffix match avoids saying 'did not change' for a crate-relative path such as `src/verify.rs`.

rejected.why: `path_of_token` removes only one trailing `:digits` (verify.rs:728-731), so `file.rs:12:5:` from a panic message keeps its `:5:`. `looks_like_path` accepts any dotted token. Both were written for verifier findings, not test output.
Names are `<binary> <test>` with no path (athena-data records.rs:881-883).

decisions.choice: Make no claim when `changed_paths` is empty, and skip checks that passed or are pre-existing.
decisions.reason: An empty list means unknown (verify.rs:165-167 treats it as not docs-only). Calling every cited path 'not changed' would then be wrong. A pre-existing check is already excused and marked, so the finding would add noise.

rejected.option: Treat an empty list as 'job changed nothing'
rejected.why: A job with an empty diff fails earlier (system-facts: empty producer diff), so an empty list in `judge` means no data.

decisions.choice: Leave crates/athena-core/src/run/checks.rs (`take_baseline`, `baseline_for`, the in-loop check at ~446-455) unchanged, though the brief lists it as a deliverable.
decisions.reason: The baseline is correct for what it does and needs no new data. The gap is in the verdict and the brief. The producer's send-back already carries the failing output tail (send_back.rs:288-308), so the producer sees the paths. Touching checks.rs would add code with no demonstration.

rejected.option: Add paths to the producer send-back through run/checks.rs and send_back.rs
rejected.why: send_back.rs is not a deliverable, and the producer already gets the output tail. It would be a second, untested path.

files.purpose: Add `FailurePaths`, `failure_paths(check, changed_paths)` and `failure_path_finding(check, changed_paths) -> Option<Finding>`; call it from `judge` for each blocking check; update the doc comment of `is_pre_existing` (it says a concurrent change 'is not separated here'); add unit tests and the `judge_changed` helper.

Compute `changed_paths` before the verifier inputs, add `verifier_check_views(check_runs, changed_paths, baseline)` that appends the finding text to the `detail` of each blocking failed check's view, and use it in place of the `check_result_view` map; reuse the same `changed_paths` for `judge`.

Add the whole-job test (`a_failing_check_citing_an_untouched_path_reaches_the_verifier_brief`) and the direct view and brief test (`a_failing_check_citing_a_changed_path_is_marked_changed_in_its_view`).
One entry under [Unreleased] / Added: the root cause, the fix, the tests, the limits, and that no refusal rule is added (0% newly refused).
Append D186 after D185 (decisions.md:5410-5432), with Case, Decision, Alternatives, Tradeoff, Reversal cost and Provenance bullets; no existing line changes.

steps: Read verify.rs:190-237, 408-472 and 717-749, run/verification.rs:56-130 and 395-430, briefs.rs:1440-1470, and the helpers in verify.rs tests (1806-2001).

In verify.rs add `const CITED_EXTENSIONS`, `const MAX_CITED_PATHS: usize = 10`, `pub struct FailurePaths { pub touched: Vec<String>, pub untouched: Vec<String> }` and `pub fn failure_paths(check: &CheckRun, changed_paths: &[String]) -> FailurePaths`. It returns an empty result when `check.passed` or `changed_paths` is empty. Otherwise it splits `output_tail` on whitespace and on `()[]{}<>,;'"`=`, takes the part before the first `:` of each token, strips `./` and a trailing `.`, and keeps it only if it is relative (no leading `/` or `~`, no `..`, no `target/` prefix), has only [A-Za-z0-9_./-] characters, and ends in an allow-listed extension with a non-empty stem. It dedupes in order of first appearance and stops at 10. A path is touched if it equals a changed path or a changed path ends with `/<path>`.

In verify.rs add `pub fn failure_path_finding(check, changed_paths) -> Option<Finding>`: None when `failure_paths` has no paths. Otherwise a Minor, `FindingSource::Athena` finding via `athena_finding`. Summary: `Check <name>: its output cites <sentence>`, with the sentence built from 'path(s) the job changed: ...' and 'path(s) the job did not change: ...'. Evidence: with untouched paths, a sentence saying a failure that cites a path outside the job's change may come from the base or from a change merged after it, that the check still fails the verdict and that the criteria are judged from the diff. With only touched paths, a sentence saying the failure may come from the job's change. In `judge`, inside the `blocking_checks` loop after the failed-tests finding (verify.rs:471), push the finding when present. Do not change `reasons`. Update the doc comment of `is_pre_existing` (verify.rs:201-202) to point to this finding.

In run/verification.rs add `pub(super) fn verifier_check_views(check_runs: &[CheckRun], changed_paths: &[String], baseline: Option<&athena_data::records::Baseline>) -> Vec<CheckResultView>`. For each run it builds `crate::verify::check_result_view(run)`; for a run that failed and is not `is_pre_existing(run, baseline)` and has a finding, it sets `detail` to the old detail, `; `, the finding's summary, `. ` and its evidence (just the finding text when the old detail is empty). In `verification_stage`, move the `changed_paths` computation (lines 409-413) above `let mut inputs`, replace the `check_runs.iter().map(check_result_view).collect()` at 74-77 with `verifier_check_views(&check_runs, &changed_paths, usable_baseline)`, and pass `&changed_paths` to `judge` as before.

In verify.rs tests add `judge_changed(baseline, checks, changed)` (like `judge_against` at 1984 with `changed_paths` set) and the tests: `failure_paths_splits_cited_paths_into_changed_and_unchanged` (the input forms listed under criterion 2, the suffix match, the cap, an empty changed list and a passed check), `a_failure_citing_a_path_the_job_did_not_change_carries_that_finding`, `a_failure_citing_a_path_the_job_changed_says_so`, and `a_pre_existing_failure_gets_no_path_finding`. Each asserts the reasons are unchanged and the finding is Minor and Athena-sourced.

In run/tests.rs add the whole-job test with `leaked_sh_check`, `recording_verifier_prompts` and `run_checked_job`, asserting on the verifier prompt, the stored `brief-verifier.md`, the Rejected state and the recorded Minor finding. Add the direct test of `verifier_check_views` plus `athena_context::briefs::verifier_brief` rendering, with a pre-existing check and a passing check getting no added text.

Append D186 to docs/decisions.md and add the CHANGELOG entry under `## [Unreleased]` / `### Added`. Both name the root cause, the files, the test commands, the limits (path citation is not proof of cause; only the last 200 lines are kept) and that the expected share of newly refused readings is 0%.

Run `cargo fmt --all`, then `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --locked -p athena-core verify`, `cargo test --locked -p athena-core a_failing_check_citing`, `cargo test --locked -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus` and `cargo test --locked`.

risks.risk: A cited path outside the job's change is not proof the job did not cause the failure; for example a test reads a doc the job's code change broke. The finding could mislead the verifier.
risks.mitigation: The wording says only that the output cites paths, and that the failure may come from the base or a concurrent change. The check still fails the verdict, it is Minor, and the brief says to judge the criteria on the diff. D186 and the CHANGELOG state this limit.

risks.risk: The path extractor matches a non-path token (a version string, a dotted identifier) or misses a form (a Windows path, a path without an allow-listed extension).
risks.mitigation: The allow-list, the exclusions and the 10-path cap are pinned by the table-driven unit test in step 6. A missed form only produces no finding, which is today's behavior.

risks.risk: Only the last 200 lines of a failed run's output are kept (run/tests.rs:5690-5696, `FAILED_TAIL_LINES`), so the failing panic line may have been cut and no paths are found.
risks.mitigation: A missing path yields no finding and changes nothing. The limit is recorded in D186. It is not widened here, because stored output sizes are governed by `failure_section`, which is another change.

risks.risk: Moving the `changed_paths` computation earlier in `verification_stage` changes the borrow of `closing.candidate`.
risks.mitigation: It is a plain clone into a `Vec<String>` before `inputs` is built, from the same expression as before (verification.rs:409-413). The compiler and the existing tests would catch an error.

risks.risk: A test fixture names `docs/design/job-planning.md` or a similar path in a check's output elsewhere, and an existing test counts findings.
risks.mitigation: I searched for exact-findings assertions (run/tests.rs:1902, verify.rs:2774-2779). Their checks print no paths or `changed_paths` is empty. The final test run covers the rest.

dependents.name: `judge` findings list now may hold one more Minor Athena finding per blocking failed check
dependents.test: a_failing_check_citing_an_untouched_path_reaches_the_verifier_brief (run/tests.rs, new) and the existing verify tests `the_finding_for_a_failed_check_separates_new_from_base_failures` (verify.rs:2738), which stays exact because its output is empty

dependents.name: the stored verification record's findings
dependents.reason: A Finding with source Athena and severity Minor is an existing shape (verify.rs:291-299). No record field, schema or `check_record_file` rule changes, so old and new records parse alike.

dependents.name: finding severity filter
dependents.reason: `finding_blocks` keeps only Blocker and Major (verify.rs:688-690). The new finding is Minor, so retry decisions, 'content-only' routing and the hold rules never see it, even though its summary cites docs paths.

dependents.name: finding source filter
dependents.reason: `usable` drops every finding whose source is Athena (evidence_labels.rs:322), so the new finding never becomes evidence for a cause.

dependents.name: findings listed in an event's `what`
dependents.reason: It lists only Blocker and Major findings and the failed checks that are not pre-existing, so the Minor finding is not added to introspection text.

dependents.name: count of minor findings in a landing body
dependents.reason: It is built only for a pass. A blocking failed check always fails the verdict (verify.rs:659-663), and a pre-existing check gets no finding, so a landing body never counts the new finding.

dependents.name: `judge` with an empty changed-path list or empty output
dependents.reason: An empty `changed_paths` or empty `output_tail` yields no finding, so these tests are unaffected.

dependents.name: producer send-back of a failing check
dependents.reason: Not changed. `is_pre_existing` and `CheckFailure::of` keep their signatures and behavior, and the producer already receives the output tail. run/checks.rs is read only.

dependents.name: `is_pre_existing` and `mark_pre_existing`
dependents.reason: Not changed. The new function is separate and only reads `CheckRun.passed` and `output_tail`. A timeout check (note, no output) has no paths and gets no finding.

dependents.reason: No briefs.rs change. The text goes into `detail`, which is already printed, so the brief shapes and the context crate's tests are unchanged. A reused failed check keeps its tail and names, with the path text added to its `detail`.

dependents.reason: No prompt file, brief constant or system-facts line changes. The finding text is added to the verifier's input at run time, outside the budgeted sets (system facts: briefs sit outside the sets).

dependents.name: refusal and matching rules
dependents.dependent: crates/athena-core/tests/refusal_corpus.rs and the reading and admission rules
dependents.reason: No reading, admission or verdict rule is added or changed. The extractor feeds only a Minor informational finding and the brief text, and `reasons` is unchanged, so the expected share of newly refused readings is 0%. No corpus case maps to it.

dependents.name: other modes reaching `verification_stage`
dependents.dependent: max_concurrency / parallel drain, `athena land`, nested runs (`self.nested`, run/verification.rs:422), resumed jobs (`recorded_checks`, run/mod.rs:2149-2186)
dependents.reason: All reach the same `verification_stage` and `judge` and read only the check records and `closing.candidate`. A nested run records placeholder checks that pass, so no finding appears. A resumed job reuses recorded passing checks. If `closing.candidate` is `None`, `changed_paths` is empty and no claim is made. `[parallel] max_concurrency` only runs several jobs at once and shares no state with this code.

demonstrations.method: Read the CHANGELOG entry and D186 in the final diff.
demonstrations.observes: Both texts name the root cause: the baseline holds only base-commit failures, there is no mapping from the paths in a failing check's output to the job's changed paths, so a concurrent-change failure looks like the job's own. Both name `failure_paths` in verify.rs as the fix and say no refusal rule is added.

demonstrations.method: Run the verify unit tests, which include `failure_paths_splits_cited_paths_into_changed_and_unchanged`. It calls `failure_paths` directly on a CheckRun whose `output_tail` holds these forms: `thread 'x' panicked at crates/athena-core/src/a.rs:12:5:`, `--> src/lib.rs:3:1`, `docs/design/job-planning.md:6`, a backticked path, `./README.md`, a bare `Cargo.toml`, and a path repeated. It also holds the excluded forms `/rustc/abc/library/core.rs:1:1`, `https://x.org/a.md`, `tests::a`, `took 1.5s`, `target/debug/x.rs:1` and `../x.rs:1`. Then run `cargo test --locked -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus` as a regression guard that no reading rule changed. The extractor is not a reading rule, so no corpus case maps to it and no case is added.
demonstrations.observes: The extractor returns the relative, allow-listed paths in order of first appearance, without line numbers or duplicates. A path equal to, or suffix-matched by, a changed path is in `touched`; the others are in `untouched`. Every excluded form is absent. An empty changed-path list or a passed check gives an empty result. The existing reason assertions (`check test failed` once, `reasons.len() == 1` at verify.rs:2741-2765) still pass, which shows the reasons are unchanged. I read no corpus case ids and cite none.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point `verify::failure_paths` (step 1 adds it) and `judge` (exists, verify.rs:408). Fixture: the existing test helpers `check`, `failing` and `judge_against` (verify.rs:1806-2001), with `output_tail` set on a CheckRun. Nothing is faked.

demonstrations.method: The new test `a_failure_citing_a_path_the_job_did_not_change_carries_that_finding` builds a failing `test` check whose `output_tail` is `thread 'x' panicked at docs/design/job-planning.md:6:1:` and whose `failed_tests` has one name. It builds a baseline with `baseline_with` that has the same check passing, so the failure is not pre-existing, and sets `changed_paths = ["crates/athena-core/src/verify.rs"]`. It then calls `judge` through a new helper `judge_changed(baseline, checks, changed)`.
demonstrations.observes: final_verdict is Fail; the reasons are exactly ["check test failed"]; one extra Minor Athena finding says the failure cites docs/design/job-planning.md, which the job did not change. A pre-existing failure with the same output gets no such finding.
demonstrations.fails_without: On the base tree `judge` (verify.rs:447-472) adds no finding for the cited path, so the test's assertion that a Minor Athena finding names `docs/design/job-planning.md` as one the job did not change fails. It compiles on the base because it uses only `judge`, `VerdictInputs`, `CheckRun` and `Baseline`. The new test asserts final_verdict == Fail, the reason `check test failed` appears exactly once, the reasons list has no new entry, and the finding is Minor, Athena-sourced and names the path with 'did not change'.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point `verify::judge` with `VerdictInputs.changed_paths` and `.baseline`, both existing fields (verify.rs:153-188). Fixture: `check`, `failing`, `baseline_with` (exist, verify.rs:1806, 1835, 1973), plus a new helper `judge_changed` (step 6 adds it). The baseline is injected through `VerdictInputs.baseline`. No double; the logic under test is in `judge`.

demonstrations.method: The new test `a_failure_citing_a_path_the_job_changed_says_so` uses the same fixture. The output cites `crates/athena-core/src/verify.rs:2700:5` and `docs/design/job-planning.md:6`, and `changed_paths` is `["crates/athena-core/src/verify.rs"]`. It asserts the finding's summary contains 'the job changed crates/athena-core/src/verify.rs' and, for the second path, 'the job did not change docs/design/job-planning.md'. A second case cites only the changed path and asserts the evidence says the failure may come from the job's change. A third case, with `changed_paths` empty, asserts there is no finding.
demonstrations.observes: The finding reports the touched and untouched paths separately. A touched-only failure never says 'did not change'. An empty list gives no finding.
demonstrations.fails_without: On the base tree no path finding exists, so the assertion that the finding says the job changed `crates/athena-core/src/verify.rs` fails. It also fails if the function treated every cited path as unchanged.
demonstrations.seam: Same as criterion 3: `judge` plus `judge_changed`. Both fixtures are added in step 6.

demonstrations.method: Two tests in crates/athena-core/src/run/tests.rs. (a) `a_failing_check_citing_an_untouched_path_reaches_the_verifier_brief` runs a whole fake job with `run_checked_job` and `recording_verifier_prompts`, using a check from `leaked_sh_check` (run/tests.rs:4493). On the candidate README (`grep -q 'A demo' README.md`) the script echoes `thread 'x' panicked at docs/design/job-planning.md:6:1:` and `see README.md:1` and exits 1. The base script (`base_script()`) edits README.md, as in the test at run/tests.rs:5640. (b) `a_failing_check_citing_a_changed_path_is_marked_changed_in_its_view` calls `verifier_check_views` directly and also feeds the result to `athena_context::briefs::verifier_brief`.
demonstrations.observes: In (a) the verifier prompt holds the finding text, with docs/design/job-planning.md under 'did not change' and README.md under 'the job changed'. The stored `brief-verifier.md` holds it too, the final state is Rejected, and `verification.findings` holds the same Minor finding. In (b) a pre-existing failing check and a passing check get no added text, and `verifier_brief` prints the text inside the parentheses after `failed`.
demonstrations.fails_without: On the base tree `verification_stage` builds the brief from `check_result_view` alone, so `brief-verifier.md` and the verifier prompt do not contain the untouched-path text. The test asserts they do, so it fails without the change. The unit test of `verifier_check_views` does not compile without it.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points are the whole run `Athena::go` (exists; used by `run_checked_job` at run/tests.rs:4561) and `verifier_check_views` (step 3 adds it, called from `verification_stage`). demonstrations.method: Read the diff. CHANGELOG.md gains one entry under `## [Unreleased]` / `### Added`. docs/decisions.md gains only an appended `## D186` section, with Case, Decision, Alternatives, Tradeoff, Reversal cost and Provenance bullets in the form of D185 (decisions.md:5410-5432).
